method.method_draft: First read the molecular graph from the image rather than the arrows. Start at Ar1, encode it as a phenyl ring, attach it to the azo nitrogen sequence N=N, then continue to the central carbon bearing Ar2 as a phenyl branch. From that carbon continue to the adjacent carbon bearing the ester branch C(=O)OR2 and the R1-substituted imine/hydrazone branch. Convert Ar1 and Ar2 to c1ccccc1/c2ccccc2 and convert R1, R2, and X into wildcard substituent notation. Linearizing this connectivity gives c1ccccc1N=NC(c2ccccc2)C(C(=O)O[2*])C(*)=NN*.

planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the non-arrow structure: an Ar1–N=N fragment bonded to a central carbon that also bears H and Ar2; that central carbon is bonded to an adjacent carbon bearing an ester group C(=O)OR2; the adjacent carbon is connected to an imine/hydrazone-like branch with R1 on the carbon and =N–NH–X/NN substituent. Ignore the curved arrows and charge/proton-transfer annotations except insofar as they do not change the drawn atom connectivity requested.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the output must be a SMILES string and that all curved arrows in the transition-state drawing should be ignored when determining the static connectivity.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply SMILES syntax rules: aromatic phenyl rings are written as c1ccccc1; azo linkage is N=N; branches are parenthesized; ester is C(=O)O[2*] for OR2; generic substituents such as R1 and X are represented with wildcard atoms such as * or N*. Preserve the drawn single/double bond pattern when linearizing the molecule.
